elements.element: Each Party's aggregate liability is subject to the cap on a mutual basis.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 applies the aggregate liability cap to “each Party.”

elements.element: The fee-based limb of the cap includes Fees both paid and payable.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 includes only Fees “actually paid” and omits Fees payable.

elements.element: The fee-based limb uses the twelve months preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 uses the twelve months “preceding the event,” not the twelve months preceding the claim.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of the applicable twelve-month Fees and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 contains no USD 1,000,000 floor or greater-of formulation.

elements.element: Indirect damages are excluded for both Parties.
elements.evidence: Section 21.2 provides that “neither Party” is liable for indirect damages, subject to Excluded Claims and legal excludability.

elements.element: Consequential damages are excluded for both Parties.
elements.evidence: Section 21.2 provides that “neither Party” is liable for consequential damages, subject to Excluded Claims and legal excludability.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Sections 21.1 and 21.3 exclude a Party's breach of confidentiality obligations from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for breach of data-protection obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Sections 21.1 and 21.3 exclude a Party's breach of data-protection obligations from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for breach of security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Sections 21.1 and 21.3 exclude a Party's breach of security obligations from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for indemnification obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Sections 21.1 and 21.3 exclude each Party's indemnification obligations from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Sections 21.1 and 21.3 exclude gross negligence from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Sections 21.1 and 21.3 exclude wilful misconduct from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for fraud is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Sections 21.1 and 21.3 exclude fraud from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for infringement of the other Party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Sections 21.1 and 21.3 exclude infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property from the cap.

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are not damages for purposes of the liability cap.
elements.evidence: Section 21.3 protects only Customer's obligation to pay “undisputed Fees for conforming Services,” rather than all Customer payment obligations.

elements.evidence: Section 21.1 caps liability at Fees actually paid in the twelve months preceding the event.

elements.element: Liability for indemnification obligations is carved out of the cap.

result.reason: The redline reaches the fallback by creating a mutual twelve-month-fees cap and placing all required fallback claims outside it. It does not reach the preferred position because the cap excludes payable Fees, uses the event rather than the claim as the lookback trigger, lacks the USD 1,000,000 minimum and greater-of structure, and protects only a limited subset of Customer payment obligations. The operative edits are concise and preserve the existing exclusions and direct-damages treatment, although “preceding the event” is less precise than a claim-based trigger.
